acceptedClaims.declaredStatement: For the half-skew BSSC product channel P^{otimes 2}, every finite Marton law whose induced super-input X_1X_2 is supported on at most three of {00,01,10,11} has unnormalized Marton sum value strictly below 0.695 bits. A fair one-letter randomized-time-division schedule with reflected rational conditional priors 1/6 and 5/6, repeated independently twice, has exact unnormalized value B_{1/6}=2h_2(1/4)+h_2(1/12)-h_2(5/12)-1/3>0.7231 bits. Therefore every strict two-letter Marton improvement over twice the optimal one-letter randomized-time-division value must assign positive mass to all four super-input symbols. Quantitatively, every such improving witness must assign mass greater than 1/180 to each of 00 and 11 and mass greater than 1/325 to each of 01 and 10. This is a support-pruning theorem for the two-letter Marton functional, not a full-support no-gain theorem or an unrestricted capacity converse.
acceptedClaims.validitySummary: The supplied argument establishes the claim without external dependencies. It derives the universal bound M≤G(P_S)+2r, maximizes G on both symmetry classes of three-symbol faces to obtain M<0.695, constructs the finite independently repeated randomized-time-division witness with exact value B_{1/6}=0.723171009237413…>0.7231, and uses indicator decomposition plus certified face bounds to prove the strict mass floors P_S(00),P_S(11)>1/180 and P_S(01),P_S(10)>1/325 for every witness strictly improving on twice the optimal one-letter RTD value.
scopeQualifications: It is a support-pruning theorem only; it does not prove that full-support Marton laws cannot yield a gain.
It is not a converse for unrestricted broadcast coding or a determination of unrestricted sum capacity.
The numerical attestation supports the finite algebraic and numerical inequalities, while the universal Marton reduction and calculus steps are established in the written proof.
The result concerns the unnormalized two-letter Marton functional for the half-skew BSSC product channel.
